behavior: A payer-chooses invoice takes the option paid first only after every option's chain was read past that payment
acceptance: With a full payment on one chain and later dust on a chain the worker reads first, the full payment's option is chosen and paid; the dust is held.

Until every other enabled option chain was scanned past the earliest transfer's block time (about one round), no option is chosen and no deposit of the invoice is booked; the pay page and the owner page call money on another option held only once an option is chosen.
notes: 2026-10-19 review fail by reviewer: Blocker: apps/backend/internal/ledger/process.go:87-98 waits until every enabled option chain is FINAL past the first transfer. The race is chain read order inside one round, and acceptance 2 asks for 'scanned past'. Final past makes every payer-chooses payment wait for the slowest chain's finality: Base 15-25 min, Arbitrum 16-19 min (docs/spikes/s4-chains.md). Arc and Tempo payments were paid at once before. During the wait chosen_id is null and the paid option stays open, not detected. The readers then show wrong state, and none were fixed or named (AGENTS.md rule). Pay page (apps/web/src/features/pay/components/pay-invoice.tsx:537-546) tells the payer the money went to another option, is held, and to ask for it back. The option picker stays open, which invites a second payment. Owner detail (apps/web/src/features/invoices/components/invoice-detail.tsx:301-310) lists it under 'Held for the payer'. If the main option's chain passes expiry, an on-time full payment shows as expired, then flips to paid. A scratch probe confirmed this: shown status expired, optionLocked false, option open; paid once the third chain was final. Fix: gate on each chain's scanned head time (store it on chain_cursors), so the wait is about one round. Or keep final, fix or name the readers, and state the wait in R-119. Minor: one stalled enabled chain now blocks every payer-chooses invoice with money on any chain; past the 24 h settle window the creator can't be paid. Disabling the chain unblocks it; say so in money-safety.md. Minor: '<' treats a chain final at the same second as past; Arc and Tempo make several blocks per second. Use '<=' to wait for strictly past. Minor: api.md says 'read past', R-119 and architecture.md say 'final past'. architecture.md 'open -> detected (a transfer seen)' no longer holds during the wait. R-119's first sentence is 28 words (D-84). Fine: the choice is still made under the main row lock, and only the worker calls Process. ProcessChain still selects the waiting invoice each round. A missing cursor can't happen, since options need a cursor at creation. Disabled chains are skipped. Ran: go test ./internal/ledger ./internal/worker ./internal/watcher, all pass. The new test fails against origin/main process.go in a scratch copy (dust chosen). Verify log 2026-10-19T19:19:42Z: all checks passed.

2026-10-19 review pass by reviewer: Re-review of 9ff04e3. The blocker is fixed. The choice now waits until every other enabled option chain was scanned strictly past the first transfer (chain_cursors.last_scanned_time, migration 00047). That is about one round, not 15-25 min of finality. The pay page and owner page call money on another option held only once optionLocked. Activity already treats a null chosen_id as not held. Watcher: the scanned time comes from the latest block's header. It falls back to the finalized time when that header is missing, which only makes the choice wait longer. The cursor CASE matches last_scanned_block. The choice is still made under the main row lock, and only the worker calls Process. Minor: the gate trusts one scan's eth_getLogs answer up to latest. The docs say one answer can miss a log (lagging node, RescanDepth). A missed payment log on another chain can still let later money win. That money is held for the payer, not lost. Consider naming this in money-safety.md accepted risks. Minor: the ledger test's scanned helper sets scanned and finalized times to the same value. So no committed test pins 'waits for the scan, not finality' or the same-second rule. My scratch probe confirmed both: scanned to 1400 waits, scanned to 1401 with finalized at 200 chooses and pays. No web test covers 'no held text before the lock'. Minor: R-119's first sentence is 26 words, and the architecture.md bullet's first sentence is about 28 (D-84). architecture.md line 197 lists chain_cursors without last_finalized_time and last_scanned_time. Ran: go test ./internal/ledger ./internal/worker ./internal/watcher, all pass. The new test fails against origin/main process.go in a scratch copy (dust chosen). Verify log 2026-10-19T19:35:54Z: all checks passed. Scratch copies removed; working tree clean.
